why_not_adjudicable: These are v1 reviews. The current schema (v2) requires per-sample contextual-validity verdicts, exact clause coverage and dispatch-bound provenance, which a v1 reviewer was never asked for and which therefore cannot be recovered from a v1 record without inventing them. Every node listed here still owes a fresh blind re-review. This file exists so that the previous programme's findings remain visible as a QUEUE while none of them counts as evidence.
required_work: 99 node(s) need a fresh blind review filed at schema_version 2. Rebuild a packet with: python -m backend.app.practice_gen.validation.judgment_packets --node <node_id>

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The samples do what the wording asks: they describe a multi-step movement in a single direction and require the resulting location, with the total displacement recovered from two consecutive steps.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Up and down slides appear only in items that ask for the name of the movement; every item that actually computes a landing position runs horizontally along marks or spaces, so the vertical case is never taken through to a described effect.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: One distractor list offers dilation alongside rotation and reflection. Dilation is nowhere near Grade 2 vocabulary and its presence teaches nothing, since no pupil at this level can reject it for a reason.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four distinct demands are present across the seeds: where the figure ends up, what the movement is called, how far it travelled altogether, and whether size or shape is preserved.

competency_alignment.rationale: Harder seeds lengthen the two hops and shift the starting mark, which is exactly the quantity a pupil must track to describe a multi-step slide; nothing unrelated is being varied.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Slide lengths stay between one and four spaces and starting marks stay in single digits, which suits a Quarter 1 figure-on-a-grid task.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Comparison is well served, but the measuring half of this competency survives in only two items, both asking how long the object is. Eight of the ten samples hand the pupil two finished numbers, which is number comparison and needs no measuring tool at all.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Longer and shorter are both asked, and centimetres and metres both appear in the comparison items, yet the actual measuring items only ever request an answer in cm. Measuring a length in metres with a tool is never generated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: One-step comparisons of two stated lengths, phrased in a single short sentence with familiar school objects, are well within what a Grade 2 Quarter 2 pupil can hold.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three formatters are used but only two situations exist: two objects side by side, or two distances from a landmark. A measuring item where the pupil reads a scale appears just twice and with word-for-word identical wording both times.

competency_alignment.rationale: The step up in the later seeds is purely numeric, moving from a pencil at 10 and a ruler at 15 to distances of 82 and 37. Comparing larger integers is a number-sense axis, not a measurement one, so the added difficulty does not build this competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Object lengths sit in the tens of centimetres and distances in the tens of metres, which are believable magnitudes for the classroom objects and school landmarks named.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Identifying the right unit is handled thoroughly, but the competency also says to use that unit, and no sample ever asks the pupil to record or state a measurement once the unit is chosen. Every item stops at the choice.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both halves of the wording are populated: lengths of objects such as a spoon, a book and an eraser, and distances between two named places such as a gate and a library, with correct answers falling on both cm and m.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: A binary unit choice about familiar objects is appropriate here, and the magnitudes supplied in the blank-style stems, such as about 28 for a basketball court, give the pupil a usable cue without arithmetic.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All twelve samples are the same two-way choice carrying the identical pair of filler options, either works and neither works. There is no ranking item, no odd-one-out, and no item where a wrong unit has to be corrected.

competency_alignment.rationale: The objects and distances chosen do move across the plausible range, from an eraser up to a basketball court and a house-to-church distance, so the progression tracks the size judgment this competency trains.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Each stated magnitude is realistic for the thing named, with small objects in the single and low double digits and distances of 50 and 150 for places that are genuinely that far apart.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Not one sample asks the pupil to estimate. Every item supplies an exact measurement and then asks for it rounded to the nearest 5 or nearest 10. Rounding a number already given is arithmetic on a numeral; estimating a length or distance is judging an unmeasured quantity, and that verb is never exercised.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Credit where due, all three combinations the wording names do occur: centimetres for objects, metres for objects, and metres for distance. But each is delivered through the one rounding task, so the sub-cases differ only in the unit word.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The values to be rounded stay between 14 and 35 and the rounding grain is 5 or 10, which is a reasonable arithmetic load for this grade even though it is the wrong task for this competency.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Twelve samples, one template. Each names an object or a school-to-school distance, states a measurement, and asks about how many units that is once rounded. Nothing varies except the noun, the number and the rounding grain.

competency_alignment.rationale: The only thing that changes between an easy and a hard seed is whether the target is the nearest 5 or the nearest 10. That is a rounding-precision axis; it does not deepen any estimating skill because no estimating is taking place.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Lengths in the twenties of centimetres and distances in the teens to thirties of metres are appropriate magnitudes for the rulers, storybooks, hallways and fences described.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Each sample is a genuine situation requiring a length or distance calculation, not a bare sum dressed up: objects laid end to end, two walked legs of a journey, and one place being farther from a gate than another.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both problem structures a competency like this needs are present in quantity. Joining appears through combined length and total distance walked, and comparing appears through how many metres farther and how many cm longer.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Single-step problems with two-digit quantities, named children and school landmarks match Quarter 2 of Grade 2; the subtraction cases such as 43 minus 19 involve regrouping but remain within reach.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three distinct situation types recur across the seeds rather than one, and they alternate between centimetre object problems and metre distance problems, with both cloze and multiple-choice presentation.

competency_alignment.rationale: The later seeds raise the operands toward sums in the fifties and sixties while keeping the same length and distance reasoning intact, so difficulty grows along the competency rather than beside it.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Totals stay below one hundred, with objects sized in tens of centimetres and walks of a few tens of metres, all plausible for the classroom and schoolyard settings used.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The wording is about the duration of an event, yet no event is ever named. Each item gives two bare dates and asks how many days or weeks lie between them inclusive, so nothing is being described as having a duration.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Every weeks item spans an exact multiple of seven days, seven, fourteen or twenty-one, so a duration expressed as weeks together with leftover days never appears. The and part of the days and/or weeks wording is unproduced.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Counting inclusive days inside one month, with all spans kept within a single calendar page and never crossing a month boundary, is a fair demand for the fourth quarter of Grade 2.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: All fourteen samples share one formatter and one sentence, opening by directing the pupil to look at the month's calendar and closing with the same inclusive phrasing. Only the month, the two dates, and the choice of the word days or weeks ever change.

competency_alignment.rationale: Widening the date span and switching the requested unit from days to weeks are both legitimate ways to press on calendar reading, so the difficulty axis does belong to this competency even though the presentation does not vary.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: No span exceeds twenty-one days and every one lies inside a single month of 2025, which keeps the answers to small whole numbers of days or weeks as the competency implies.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both verbs are served. Reading appears through items asking what time the clock shows, and writing appears through items asking the pupil to set the clock to a stated time, and a.m. or p.m. is attached in every single case.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The minute values cluster heavily on the hour, the half hour and forty-five past. Quarter past and five past never occur as targets, and only three distinct clock faces are ever read, so the reading direction is thinly covered against eight setting items.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: One item asks the pupil to set the clock to show 12:00 a.m. Midnight against noon is the single hardest a.m. and p.m. case there is, and dropping it in without scaffolding is a real stretch for this grade.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only two presentations exist across twelve samples, and eight of them open with the same instruction to set the clock. No item connects a clock time to a daily routine or asks for a time to be written in words.

competency_alignment.rationale: The variation across seeds is the hour and minute values chosen and the a.m. or p.m. label, which is precisely what a pupil must control to read and write analog time.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every target is a valid twelve-hour clock time on a five-minute boundary, and nothing strays into seconds or twenty-four-hour notation that would sit above this grade.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The samples land squarely on elapsed time and each of the three parenthesised sub-domains is exercised, including one where a class runs from 9:15 a.m. to 9:35 a.m. and one where a train journey's start must be recovered from its end and its length.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Minutes within an hour, whole hours within a day, days within a week, and timetables all appear, and the direction is varied too: some items ask for the duration, others for the end time, and one for the start time.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Durations stay under an hour for the minute items and the day-of-week items sit inside one week; the hardest case, a practice beginning at 10:25 a.m. and lasting 55 minutes, requires crossing an hour but nothing more.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Presentation genuinely shifts: a two-row bus timetable, a class schedule with subject names, plain start-and-end narratives, and weekday-spanning events all appear, across both cloze and multiple-choice.

competency_alignment.rationale: The harder seeds add a crossing of noon and an unknown start time rather than merely enlarging numbers, so the progression targets the elapsed-time reasoning itself.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Elapsed intervals run from twenty minutes up to six hours and event lengths from two to four days, all of which stay inside the minutes-in-an-hour, hours-in-a-day and days-in-a-week bounds the competency states.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both the identifying and the explaining verbs are present. Some items ask which description best fits a rim or an edge, while others ask directly how a straight line differs from a curved one and why a given edge carries its name.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The three-dimensional half of the wording rests on a box and a ball only. No object is used that carries flat and curved surfaces at the same time, which is the case where a pupil must actually separate the two ideas rather than match one label.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Explanations are offered as complete short sentences about bending and not bending, which is the right level; the pupil recognises a correct explanation rather than composing one.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every one of the nine samples is a multiple-choice item, and several close with the same request for the best description. There is no sorting task, no true-or-false, and no item that asks a pupil to find an example of their own.

competency_alignment.rationale: The variation across seeds moves between lines and surfaces and between naming and justifying, both of which are written into this competency rather than borrowed from a neighbouring one.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: This competency names no quantity or ceiling and the samples introduce none; the items remain entirely qualitative, which is correct for it.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency turns on measuring a figure with appropriate tools, and not one sample involves a tool or an unmeasured figure. Every item states the side lengths in the sentence and asks for the perimeter, which is arithmetic on given numbers rather than measurement.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The wording says plane figure in general, but only triangles, squares and rectangles are generated, and no item requires the pupil to obtain a dimension that was not already printed.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Adding three sides or doubling a length and a width, with side values no larger than twenty-one, is arithmetic a Grade 2 pupil in the fourth quarter can carry out.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Thirteen of the fourteen samples are the bare what is its perimeter frame, and the sample set duplicates the neighbouring find-the-perimeter node almost seed for seed, which means this node contributes no presentation of its own.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty grows only by enlarging side lengths, moving a square's side from three up to seventeen. No seed increases any measuring demand, because there is no measuring demand to increase.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Side lengths run from one to twenty-one and perimeters top out below seventy, which keeps the addition inside a sensible range for this grade.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Each sample asks for the perimeter of one of the three figures the competency names, and the computations are correct throughout, including the triangle cases where three unequal sides must be summed.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Triangles, squares and rectangles are all generated repeatedly, with squares given by a single side, rectangles given by two sides, and triangles given by three, so each figure's own perimeter rule gets exercised.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The heaviest item asks for four times seventeen by repeated addition of a side, which is within the fourth-quarter range; all other cases are sums of small two-digit values.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Apart from a single garden item asking how much fencing goes all the way around, every sample is the identical bare question about a figure's perimeter. No diagram-led, missing-side or comparison presentation occurs.

competency_alignment.rationale: Across all fourteen seeds the four options sit within three units of the key, so a pupil who forgets to double a rectangle's sides finds no option matching their error and simply guesses; the option set is tuned to near-misses rather than to the misconceptions this competency should surface.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Side lengths stay between one and twenty-one, and the largest perimeter reached is sixty-eight, comfortably inside Grade 2 addition range.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Each item embeds a perimeter calculation in a real reason to go around a shape, asking how much fencing or edging is needed, and all three named figures carry their own situation.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Only the forward direction is generated. No sample supplies a perimeter and asks for a missing side, and none requires two steps such as comparing the fencing for two plots, which a solve-problems competency should reach.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: One-step problems in a garden setting with side lengths in metres and totals below seventy match what a fourth-quarter Grade 2 pupil can handle without scaffolding.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: There are effectively two sentences in the whole set, a rectangular or square garden needing fencing and a triangular flower bed needing edging. Every context is a garden, and no non-garden situation or diagram-led version appears.

competency_alignment.rationale: The later seeds enlarge the plot dimensions, up to a square garden with a side of seventeen metres, while holding the perimeter reasoning constant, so the ramp belongs to this competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Plot dimensions run from one to twenty-one metres and every total stays under seventy, which suits both the arithmetic level and the realism of a school garden.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Counting by ones is what this competency names, and several samples do not do it. Two items step by hundreds and one steps by twos, which is a different skill wearing the same what comes next wrapper.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Only forward counting is ever produced. Nothing counts backward, nothing counts on from a stated number toward a stated stop, and no item asks for a number that precedes the given run rather than follows it.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Four-term runs with one blank, in three-digit numbers, are well matched to the opening quarter of Grade 2, and the narrated version naming a child counting forward adds context without adding reading burden.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four presentations occur across the seeds: a marked number line, a sequence with a trailing blank, a sequence introduced as a missing number, and a short narrative about someone counting aloud.

competency_alignment.rationale: Four of the fourteen samples are skip-counting sequences, including one running 0, 100, 200, 300 and another running 400, 500, 600, 700. Skip counting is the subject of a separate competency in this same quarter, so a substantial share of this node's difficulty is being varied on a neighbouring node's axis.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency's ceiling is a thousand, yet the counting-by-ones items peak in the five hundreds; only the skip-counting intruders reach the upper hundreds, so the by-ones skill is never taken near the stated top of range.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both directions the wording implies are generated: numerals turned into words, as with 470 and 587, and words turned back into numerals, as with seven hundred ten and three hundred fifty.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Numbers with an internal zero, such as 605 and 710, are included, which is good, but the whole set lives between 203 and 821. Nothing in the nine hundreds is generated and the thousand itself, the stated endpoint, never appears in either direction.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Three-digit number words with hyphenated tens such as eighty-seven are the correct load for Quarter 1 here, and no stem requires more than one number to be handled at a time.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three formatters are used, but all three true-or-false instances are keyed False. A pupil who simply answers False every time scores full marks on that presentation, which makes it a degenerate variant rather than a third way of testing the skill.

competency_alignment.rationale: The distractors are built from real confusions this competency must clear, such as offering seventy-four against 470 and 53 against three hundred fifty, so the harder options probe place-value reading rather than an unrelated axis.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every value handled is a three-digit numeral, which sits inside the range this competency sets even though the very top of that range goes untested.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The affirmative items genuinely illustrate the properties, but each negative one works by quietly substituting a different addend, as when 168 + 511 is set against 511 + 137. The pupil answers by spotting that a number changed, not by reasoning about order or grouping, so the false cases do not teach the property they are attached to.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three properties the wording lists are produced: adding zero in several forms, reordering two addends, and regrouping three addends with parentheses, each appearing across multiple seeds.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Parenthesised grouping is demanded by the competency itself, and the pupil is only ever asked whether two arrangements match rather than to evaluate both sides, which keeps the load manageable at this grade.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four presentations occur: a true-or-false statement, a same-or-not comparison, a fill-in-the-total, and an error-detection item where a named pupil's answer must be checked.

competency_alignment.rationale: The zero property gets the richer treatment, appearing as a cloze and as an error-detection item, while order and grouping only ever arrive as a same-or-not judgment. Applying those two properties, as opposed to judging them, is never required.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every sum stays at or below a thousand, with the largest pairs such as 976 plus 3 and 783 plus 213 approaching but not breaching that ceiling.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both directions are attempted, building a model for a stated numeral and naming the numeral a model shows, but one options list places 20 among three three-digit choices, so that item can be narrowed without looking at the blocks at all.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The wording promises a variety of concrete and pictorial models, and exactly two ever appear: base-10 blocks and a number line. No place-value chart, bundled objects, money or expanded notation is generated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Three-digit values represented on blocks or a marked line, with one instruction per item, are the right demand for the opening quarter of Grade 2.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Five of the eight samples are number-line items, and two of them repeat word for word the question asking what number is marked on the number line. The blocks presentation carries the remaining three.

competency_alignment.rationale: The numerals chosen deliberately include hard representation cases such as 203 with an empty tens column and 470 with an empty ones column, which is the right axis for a representation competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: All eight values are three-digit numerals between 203 and 821, sitting inside the thousand ceiling this competency sets.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The samples do what skip counting requires, completing a four-term run at a constant step, and the runs are placed so that some cross a hundred boundary, as with the sequence ending 298 and continuing to 300.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency names six step sizes and only five are generated. Twos, fives, tens, twenties and fifties all appear, but not a single sample counts by 100s. Ironically the hundreds runs surface in the neighbouring count-to-1000 node instead, so this sub-case is not merely rare here, it is absent.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: A four-term run with one blank is the right structure for Quarter 1, and the narrated version about someone counting forward by five from 875 adds a context without lengthening the reasoning.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three presentations recur: a marked number line, a sequence with a trailing blank, and a short story about a child counting aloud, spread across cloze, multiple-choice and read-based formats.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty varies by step size and by where the run sits relative to a hundred boundary, both of which are the genuine sources of difficulty in skip counting.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency bars going beyond a thousand and nothing does; the highest sequence ends at 895 and the fifties run stops at 750.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every sample is a genuine ordering task with a correctly sorted key, and the and vice versa clause is honoured by items that ask for largest to smallest as often as smallest to largest.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both directions appear repeatedly, set sizes range from three to five numbers, and the thousand itself is included in several sets, so the top of the stated range is actually exercised rather than approached.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Arranging at most five three-digit numbers is a reasonable Quarter 1 demand, and the contextual versions about counting seashells or stickers collected by friends stay short enough not to add a reading burden.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Two situations alternate, a bare list of numbers to arrange and a collection story where several friends' counts must be ordered, and the set sizes and direction are shuffled independently of each other.

competency_alignment.rationale: The later seeds tighten the gaps between the values, with sets such as 404, 406, 399, 409 turning on the final digit, which is exactly the discrimination this competency is meant to build.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values run from the thirties up to exactly 1000 and never past it, which matches the stated ceiling and still gives a spread of magnitudes.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The ordinal language itself is handled in both surface forms, with items asking for the word describing a position and others asking for the symbol, and one item places named children in a row so a position must be located.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Positions from second through twentieth are sampled, in word form and symbol form, and in both directions: naming the ordinal for a given number and identifying which position follows another.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Single-step ordinal recognition with no arithmetic beyond adding one to a position suits the first quarter of Grade 2, and the row of six named children is short enough to hold in mind.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Most items name a position in the abstract; only the row-of-children item and the arrival-order item attach an ordinal to actual objects or people, which is what describing the position of objects calls for.

competency_alignment.rationale: The comparison item asking who arrived earlier offers 16th, 7th and 8th as alternatives when the stem mentions only two places, so three of its four options are impossible and the item collapses to a coin flip that needs no ordinal reasoning.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: No position above twentieth is used anywhere in the set, and the item asking what follows 19th lands exactly on the stated ceiling rather than crossing it.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: This competency deliberately separates the place value of a digit from the value of a digit, and the generator collapses them. Three items ask what the place value of a digit is and then key a quantity: 80 for the 8 in 285, 200 for the 2 in 250, 60 for the 6 in 160. The stem asks for one thing and the key answers another, in the exact node where the distinction is being introduced.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three sub-cases the wording lists do get generated somewhere: naming the place a digit occupies, giving the quantity a digit stands for, and returning the digit that sits in a stated place.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Three-digit numbers with one digit probed per item, including the harder zero cases in 260 and 405, is the right level; no stem asks about more than one digit at a time.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Five of the eleven samples are true-or-false items that simply restate a candidate answer and ask for a verdict, which converts an open place-value question into a yes-or-no check and removes the need to generate the answer.

competency_alignment.rationale: Because the term used in the stem does not stay fixed to the term the key answers, a pupil working through the harder seeds cannot extract a stable rule; the progression varies which digit is probed but leaves the vocabulary unreliable.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every number used is three digits, as the competency specifies, with none padded out to four or reduced to two.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The counting-up model is genuinely enacted: each item starts at a two-digit number and moves forward by a one-digit amount, and the number-line items make that hop explicit by asking where the dot lands.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Hops that stay inside a ten and hops that cross one both occur in quantity, and starting points are spread from the thirties to the nineties rather than clustering at round numbers.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: A single one-digit hop from a stated two-digit start is exactly the load this competency is written for, and the stems stay to one or two short sentences.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Five presentations appear, which is good, but all three true-or-false items are keyed False. That variant therefore rewards answering False without ever counting up, which defeats the point of including it.

competency_alignment.rationale: The difficulty ramp raises the starting number while holding the hop at a single digit, which is the right axis: the challenge in counting up is where you start, not how far you go.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: One item starts at 94 and counts up 7, landing on 101. That carries the illustration out of the two-digit territory the competency frames, and on a number-line model the crossing of a hundred is a distinctly different picture from the rest of the set.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The expanded decomposition is handed to the pupil in every single stem; no item asks them to produce it, or to express the answer in expanded form. Once the hundreds, tens and ones are written out for them, what remains is ordinary column addition, so the expanded-form method is demonstrated rather than practised.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Pairings vary usefully across the set: two-digit added to three-digit as well as three-digit to three-digit, cases that carry such as 647 and 175, cases that do not such as 240 and 670, and one pair landing exactly on a thousand.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The reading load is heavy for Quarter 1 of Grade 2. Each stem spells out two full decompositions, issues an instruction to add the place values and then find the total, and only then poses the question, which is a long text for a pupil still consolidating three-digit numerals.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four formatters are present but every one of them carries the same two-sentence decomposition preamble and the same instruction before the question, so the presentation never genuinely changes, only the answer mechanism does.

competency_alignment.rationale: The progression moves between carrying and non-carrying pairs and pushes the total toward the ceiling, both of which are the genuine difficulty sources for addition by place value.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: No total exceeds a thousand and one pair reaches it exactly, so the stated ceiling is both respected and actually tested.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The samples are addition with totals at or below a thousand and the arithmetic is sound throughout, including the pair reaching exactly a thousand and the several pairs that require carrying across two columns.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The with or without regrouping clause is honoured on both sides: pairs like 244 and 335 need no carrying while pairs like 689 and 158 need it twice, and two-digit plus three-digit combinations appear alongside three-digit pairs.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Several items tell the pupil to count up a large number of single steps on a number line, in one case moving forward 297 numbers from 634. Counting up by ones is not a usable method at that magnitude, so the instruction misdescribes what the pupil must actually do.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The presentations are genuinely diverse here: a number-line placement, a part-and-whole framing, an error-detection narrative, a true-or-false statement, a step-climbing story, and bare computation.

competency_alignment.rationale: Two samples sit outside the regrouping skill this node builds. One adds zero, which belongs to the properties competency, and the true-or-false item asserting that 633 plus 367 equals 633 is rejectable at a glance because the claimed total equals one addend.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every total stays at or under a thousand, with the largest results at 950, 931 and 906, so the ceiling is worked right up to without being crossed.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Two of the money number-line items cannot be answered from what they state. One puts the dot at 25 pesos, moves it forward 50 pesos, and keys 175; another starts at 200 pesos, moves forward 100 pesos, and keys 400. In both cases the stated start and step do not produce the keyed amount, and the correct total does not even appear among the options, so a pupil who computes properly is forced into a wrong answer.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All four parenthesised groupings are represented, but only just: centavo coins appear in a single item, peso coins in a single item, bills alone in a single item, and the combined case in one more. Three of the four sub-cases rest on one sample each.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Asking a pupil to make exactly 801 pesos using the fewest pieces possible is a minimisation problem over a mixed denomination set, which is a markedly heavier demand than totalling given bills and coins and sits above what the second quarter of Grade 2 should require.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three genuinely different demands occur: totalling a stated collection of bills and coins, constructing a target amount from pieces, and locating an amount after a jump, delivered across several formatters.

competency_alignment.rationale: One make-the-amount item is rendered with the target amount itself sitting in the options list beside near-miss values, so it can be answered by copying the figure out of the stem without assembling anything.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Peso amounts stop at exactly 1000 and never exceed it, and the centavo item stays in true coin-sized values totalling 225 centavos, which respects the ceiling the competency states.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every item sets one collection of peso denominations against another and asks which is worth more or less; both the greater-value and smaller-value directions are keyed, and I checked each key by summing the denominations named in the stem - all fourteen are arithmetically right.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The option 'They are equal' is offered in every multiple-choice item but is never once the key, so the equal-value outcome of a comparison is advertised to the student and never actually taught. competency_alignment.rationale: Sampled denominators cluster on fifths and eighths rather than stepping through the set the competency lists, so the progression varies which fraction is asked about without widening the pupil's exposure to the named family.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The eighths ceiling named by the competency is reached and no numerator exceeds its denominator anywhere in the set, so nothing strays past the similar-fraction range of this quarter.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The reading and writing directions are both generated for genuinely non-unit fractions - three eighths, five sixths, four fifths and two fourths all appear - and each notation-to-words key correctly pluralises the denominator name.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Thirds never appear in either direction despite being available in this quarter's denominator set, and one sample, 'Write one eighth in fraction notation.', is a unit fraction duplicated verbatim from the earlier read-and-write unit fractions node rather than new content for this one.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: This is the competency where correct fraction words are the object of instruction, and two option lists put a misspelled plural of half in front of the pupil, while a third offers a non-word built from 'oneths'. Printing malformed word names to a Grade 2 reader who is being taught those very names actively works against the node's purpose.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only two question shapes exist, writing a spoken name into notation and naming printed notation in words, and the second alternates between two near-identical phrasings, so there is no picture-supported or context-embedded reading of a fraction.

competency_alignment.rationale: Because some option sets mix plausible near-misses with nonsense strings, those items can be answered by discarding what is not a word rather than by reading the fraction correctly, which weakens the rung rather than building it.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Denominators stay within fourths through eighths and every numerator is smaller than its denominator, so the fractions sampled sit inside the proper similar-fraction range for this quarter.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Each item orders fractions that share a denominator, which is what similar fractions means, and I verified all eleven keys rank by numerator in the direction the stem asks - the sevenths-of-eighths and sixths chains are all correctly sequenced.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The ascending direction the competency's 'vice versa' clause requires appears in only two of eleven samples, and thirds are never used as the common denominator even though they belong to this quarter's set.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Ordering same-denominator fractions reduces to comparing whole-number numerators, which is well within Grade 2 reach, and the lists are kept to three or four entries with the direction stated up front.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The set of quarters made from 1/4, 2/4, 3/4 is reused across three seeds, and two of those are direct direction-flips of one another producing the same two answer strings, so the apparent variety overstates how many distinct items exist.

competency_alignment.rationale: Decoys are permutations that differ by adjacent swaps rather than obviously wrong lists, so success requires actually comparing numerators, and the common denominator changes between samples across fourths, fifths, sixths and eighths.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Every numerator stays below its denominator so no sample produces an improper fraction, and the denominators remain within the two-to-eight set this quarter establishes.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency verb is to collect data from experiments, but every stem hands the learner a finished tally and asks a read-off question; nothing asks the pupil to tally, record or organise the outcomes of a trial. Seed 46 goes further and asks 'How many more times did Heads land than Tails?', which is comparison of already-collected data rather than collection.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Experiment types are well spread (coin, spinner, tile-in-bag, and a die across six faces), so the competency's named examples both appear. However all three error_detect items resolve to has_error False, so 'Is Noel correct?', 'Is Dante correct?' and 'Is Jose correct?' all answer yes; the mistaken-tally case the format exists to test is never generated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Trial counts run from 10 to 25 and each category count is a one- or two-digit number, so summing four outcome counts to 30 is squarely within Grade 3 Quarter 3 addition. Sentence length stays short and the outcome vocabulary (heads, tails, spinner, face) needs no prior teaching.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four distinct response shapes appear across the seeds (cloze, mcq, true_false, error_detect) and the question itself alternates between single-category lookup, most-frequent outcome, difference between two outcomes, and total spins. That is genuine presentational range, not one template renumbered.

competency_alignment.rationale: As the seeds advance the added demand stays inside data handling itself: from naming one recorded count, to identifying the most frequent colour, to totalling every outcome. Nothing shifts the load onto an unrelated axis such as larger numerals or extra arithmetic steps.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Outcome counts never exceed 12 and totals never exceed 30, which suits an experiment with 'a small number of possible outcomes' as the competency phrases it. The six-face die item keeps each face count in single digits.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Each stem supplies the exact figures the key then repeats: 'Complete the table to show: cats: 5, dogs: 60, birds: 25, fish: 20.' has key [5, 60, 25, 20]. Whatever graphing surface sits behind the set_fill_in_blank is not visible here, so from the rendered text alone the task is transcription, and nothing in the printed item exercises scale choice, axis labelling or bar height.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three presentation modes the competency names are produced: table completion, 'Create a horizontal bar graph' and 'Create a vertical bar graph' each occur several times across the seed set, so neither orientation is neglected in favour of the other.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Category labels are familiar Grade 3 contexts (days, grade levels, flowers, sports, months) and every value is a multiple of 5 no larger than 95, which a third grader can plot on a scaled axis without decimals or awkward intervals.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Only one response format is ever emitted and the stem wording collapses into two fixed frames. There is no item that starts from raw tallies or from a written situation, and none that asks for the graph's title or labels, so the horizontal/vertical/table split is the sole axis of variety.

competency_alignment.rationale: The only thing that changes as seeds progress is the number of categories, four in most items and six in the 500-series. Presenting six bars rather than four is not a deeper grasp of tabulating or graphing; the graphing demand itself is identical throughout.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Values sit between 5 and 95 and are uniformly multiples of five, so a bar graph with an interval of 5 or 10 fits the page and matches the data ranges Grade 3 pupils are expected to graph.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Reading values, totals, extremes and differences off a display is squarely the interpretive act the competency names, and most stems do it cleanly. The two comparison items break that: 'Which is greater: grapes or apples?' names exactly two categories but is answered from a four-way list that also offers mangoes and bananas, neither of which the stem put in play. The same shape recurs on the Grade 4 versus Grade 2 item. Half the option set is dead weight, so the item tests a narrower comparison than its own wording promises.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency parenthesises 'horizontal and vertical' and names tables alongside them; all three display types are genuinely represented here, with tables appearing on four seeds, horizontal graphs on four and vertical graphs on six. Interpretation tasks also span single-cell lookup, summing every category, identifying the most and the least, and computing a difference between two named bars, so no obvious sub-case of interpreting is left ungenerated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Each stem is a two-sentence orientation-then-question pattern of roughly a dozen words, which suits a Grade 3 reader in the third quarter. The heaviest demand is 'What is the total value of all categories?', a multi-addend sum landing in the low hundreds, which is well inside third-quarter addition. No term beyond the data-handling vocabulary a Grade 3 pupil meets in this unit appears in any sample.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Orientation variety is real, but presentation variety is not: all fourteen seeds are the same read_mcq interaction, and every one opens with the identical 'Look at the' lead-in before the question clause. There is no contextualised or narrative framing anywhere in the set, and no non-selection response mode, so a pupil working through this node meets one item shape fourteen times over while only the picture underneath it changes.

competency_alignment.rationale: Harder seeds get harder by demanding more of the graph, not by importing a foreign skill: a single-category lookup sits at the easy end, a two-bar difference in the middle, and a full sum across every category at the top. That ladder is entirely built out of reading a display, which is what interpreting data means, so the escalating axis and the competency's target skill are the same thing.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Individual category values sit in the twenties and thirties, the largest quantity anywhere is the 365 total, and differences are small multiples of five. Nothing approaches or exceeds the number range a Grade 3 pupil handles by Quarter 3, and nothing is so small that reading the scale becomes trivial. The category labels are also everyday sets such as fruit, school subjects and grade levels.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every stem begins from a bar graph and poses a genuine problem on top of it rather than a bare reading: combining two categories, finding how many more one has than another, scaling by a unit price, or adding items to a category as in 'If 5 more items are added to Art, what will be the new total for Art?'. That is solving with graph data, as worded.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency restricts itself to the single bar graph, and correctly no table items appear; within that restriction both orientations are used and four distinct problem structures (join, compare, multiply by a rate, increase) are generated across the seeds.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The heaviest computation is a two-digit by one-digit product such as the Thursday item costing 5 pesos per item with key 325, which Grade 3 Quarter 3 multiplication supports. Peso pricing is a familiar local context and the stems remain single-clause.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Although the response widget is constant, the situations genuinely differ: cost problems at three different unit prices, combination totals, difference comparisons and an increase-the-category item, across flowers, subjects, weekdays, sports, months and grade levels.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty grows by adding a second operation to the graph reading, for example moving from 'How many more items were recorded for dogs than for cats?' to a unit-price total. Both ends of that progression still depend on extracting values from the bar graph, which is the competency's core.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Bar values stay in the tens and the largest derived answer is 600 from the basketball cost item, so results remain well under the 10 000 ceiling Grade 3 works within while still being large enough to be worth computing.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The five required terms are each the key of at least one item: 'certain' for the all-red spinner, 'impossible' for rolling a 7 on a six-sided die, 'less likely' and 'more likely' for the unequal ball counts, and 'equally likely' for the five-red five-blue bag. The items both describe a single outcome and compare two, matching the competency's two verbs.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Superlative and comparative forms are unevenly served. 'LEAST likely' is generated twice, but no stem ever asks which outcome is most likely as a superlative; seed 502 asks only 'Which outcome is more likely?'. The competency lists less/least and more/most as paired forms and one half of the second pair is missing.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Counts are tiny (5 red balls, 3 yellow of 5 sections, 8 goldfish) so no ratio or fraction reasoning is smuggled in, and the probability language stays qualitative, which is correct for Grade 3 where numeric probability is not yet introduced.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Ten of the eleven samples are bag-of-balls or spinner abstractions; only the aquarium tank with goldfish, guppies and an angelfish reaches the 'real-life situations' the competency demands. The format is mcq without exception, so there is no describe-in-your-own-words or true/false judgement variant.

competency_alignment.rationale: One item is internally unsound as a discriminator: the spinner with 3 yellow, 1 red and 1 green has key 'red or green' because those two tie, yet the option list also offers 'blue', a colour that is not on the spinner at all. An impossible option in a likelihood item is particularly damaging, since judging impossibility is itself part of this competency.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Section and object counts never exceed ten, which keeps every comparison decidable by direct counting rather than computation. That is the right scale for a competency whose ceiling is qualitative description, not quantification.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Covering a shape with unit tiles is exactly the illustrated activity intended, and the array items supply the picture the competency's first verb calls for. The estimation verb is where the samples drift. Stems advertise estimating, as in 'Estimate how many unit tiles cover the square in all', yet every key is the exact product and the distractors punish approximation rather than reward it: the options against the 7x4 array are 29, 25, 28 and 22, a spread no estimate could separate. Seed 502 is self-contradictory on its face, promising tiles 'fitting 3 rows and 3 columns exactly' and then asking 'About how many tiles in total will you use?'. No sampled item exercises estimating behaviour.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both shapes the competency disjoins are produced in quantity: squares turn up as 2 by 2, 3 by 3, 4 by 4, 5 by 5 and 10 by 10 tilings, while rectangles appear at 2 by 7, 5 by 3, 5 by 6 and several array sizes. The illustrated route and the verbally described route are both present too, so neither the shape sub-cases nor the two modes of presenting the tiling are missing.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Row-and-column counts stay within the multiplication facts a Grade 3 pupil is building in the opening quarter, and the reasoning is a single step from array dimensions to a count. Phrasing such as covering a shape edge-to-edge is concrete and supported by the accompanying figure. The one measurement-flavoured stem, about a garden two metres long and three metres wide tiled with one-metre squares, still reduces to counting whole tiles rather than to any formal area computation.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three different interaction types are in evidence across the seeds, and the framings genuinely differ: a figure-reading item, an impersonal description of a tiled shape, a second-person tiling narration, and a named-character situation where 'Pia wants to cover a rectangular garden'. Row-by-column orientations are also flipped between seeds rather than fixed, so the same product is met in more than one arrangement.

competency_alignment.rationale: What grows across the seeds is the size of the tiled region, from a four-tile square up to a hundred-tile square, and that growth is precisely what pushes a pupil from counting tiles one by one toward seeing the array structure. Nothing in the progression swaps in an unrelated demand such as unit conversion or perimeter; every harder seed is still a tile-covering question about a square or a rectangle.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: No side length exceeds ten and no tile count exceeds one hundred, which matches the multiplication ceiling available to a Grade 3 pupil in Quarter 1. The smallest case, a two-by-two square answering to 4, is still large enough to be a genuine array rather than a degenerate one. Distractor magnitudes, such as 200 and 40 against the hundred-tile square, stay in the same believable band.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The inductive framing is real: three worked instances are laid out and the learner must generalise, with keys of length × width for rectangles and side × side for squares, so the derivation target is correct. What is thin is the phrase the competency rests on, using square tile units. No sample shows an array, a picture, or any tiling the child performs; each stem asserts the tile count outright, so the tiles are stipulated numbers rather than units the learner covers and counts. The generalisation is therefore reached from arithmetic pattern-spotting on handed-over totals, which is a weaker route to this competency than the tile manipulation it names.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both shapes the competency names are genuinely produced, not just the easier one. Squares appear across seeds 44, 45, 500, 501 and 502 with the side × side key, and rectangles across seeds 42, 43, 46, 601, 602, 604, 605 and 606 with the length × width key, at a roughly even split. Neither sub-case is a token single appearance, and the square items use true square dimensions throughout rather than being rectangles relabelled.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Reading load sits at the upper end of what an early Grade 3 measurement lesson should carry, since each stem packs three dimension-and-total clauses before the question, but the vocabulary stays inside grade: rectangle, square, tiles, rule, and the closing Which rule always gives the number of tiles? is plainly worded. Multiplication of single-digit factors, and of ten by a single digit, is within Grade 3 reach, and the answer choices use everyday shape words rather than letter symbols, so no algebraic notation is demanded.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Thirteen samples share essentially one presentation. Twelve open with the same instruction to cover the figure and count, and only seed 502 rewords the opening to Three squares are tiled with unit squares with the closing question changed. The cloze and mcq labels make no visible difference: both render the same four rule choices. Nothing turns the task around, such as supplying the rule and asking for a tile total, and no measurement context or figure-based presentation appears anywhere. Swapping square for rectangle is the only contextual variation on offer.

competency_alignment.rationale: Across the whole set the thing that changes from seed to seed is the size of the dimensions, moving from small figures up to ten by ten, while the cognitive demand stays fixed at one generalisation step. Larger factors make the arithmetic heavier without deepening the derivation, so the progression is riding a magnitude axis rather than building the reasoning this competency targets. A genuine build here would move from small tile arrays the child can verify by counting toward figures too large to count one by one, which is what forces the multiplicative rule; that pressure is not visible in the sampled ordering.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency states no numeric ceiling, being about deriving the rule rather than about a range, so the relevant test is whether the figures stay tileable and the products stay within Grade 3 arithmetic. Dimensions run from two up to ten and totals from 4 tiles up to 100 tiles, all products of factors no larger than ten. Nothing dips so low that the pattern is trivially one instance, and nothing climbs into two-digit by two-digit territory that would outrun the quarter.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Each item asks directly for an area of a square or a rectangle and states the unit in the stem, for example asking for the area of a rectangle with sides 4 cm and 3 cm in sq cm. Stem and key agree on what is wanted throughout the sample set.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both figures and both units the competency names are generated: squares in sq cm and in sq m, rectangles in sq cm and in sq m all appear, so neither the unit pair nor the figure pair is collapsed to a single case.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Dimensions stay single-digit so the largest product is 40 from the 8 cm by 5 cm rectangle, matching the multiplication range of Grade 3 Quarter 1. Phrasings such as 'measuring 5 m on each side' are short and need no unfamiliar terms.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The stem alternates among at least four constructions: sides listed as a pair, 'a side of' for squares, an imperative to find or calculate, and an applied object, the rectangular chalkboard. Both cloze and mcq responses occur.

competency_alignment.rationale: Distractors encode the misconceptions this competency must displace: for the 4 cm by 3 cm rectangle the options include 7 and 14, that is the sum of the sides and the perimeter, so choosing wrongly diagnoses confusing area with those quantities rather than an unrelated slip.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency states no ceiling, and the chosen range of 2 to 8 units per side keeps every area between 6 and 40, which is large enough to require multiplication yet small enough to verify by tiling as the preceding node taught.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Several of the harder items do the area step for the pupil. The garden plots item supplies '(area = 30 sq m)' and '(area = 45 sq m)' and then asks only how many square metres larger one plot is, and the tiling-cost items likewise state the area before asking for a product. In those problems the area work the competency is about has already been completed in the stem.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The problem types genuinely range beyond direct computation: there are inverse items recovering a missing side from a stated area and length, a comparison of two plots, and rate-based cost problems, alongside straightforward square and rectangle areas.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Contexts are all classroom-plausible for a third grader, such as a rug, a chalkboard and a picture card, and the two-step items keep the second step to a multiplication by 5 or 10 or a subtraction, so no single problem exceeds two operations.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Both cloze and mcq are used, and the objects vary widely enough that no two sampled situations repeat; the inverse-direction postcard and poster items provide a genuinely different orientation on the same relationship.

competency_alignment.rationale: In the two cost items the options cluster within a couple of units of the key, 90 against 89, 91 and 92, and 240 against 239, 241 and 242. Those distractors reward arithmetic precision on a peso total rather than discriminating between pupils who can and cannot reason about area, which is what this competency should be measuring.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Side lengths stay between 2 and 9 metres or centimetres, and the largest answer, a tiling cost of 240 pesos, remains well inside the Grade 3 number range while giving the multi-step items something substantial to compute.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency pairs recognition using models with drawing, and the sample set is dominated by verbal definition recall such as asking what we call an exact location in space with no length or width. Only one item actually shows a model, the A-to-B diagram with an arrowhead, and drawing is only ever approached indirectly through questions about which tool or which symbol to use.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All four figures the competency lists are covered and each is probed more than once: point by the location item, line segment by the endpoint count and the ruler item, ray by the flashlight model and the one-endpoint item, and line by the no-endpoints item.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The language is concrete and grade-suitable, and the flashlight beam gives a physical anchor for the abstract idea of extending in one direction. The only mildly advanced notion, extending forever, is phrased in everyday words rather than as infinity.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every sample is mcq, and three stems are emitted twice with only the option order changed: the flashlight beam item, the exact-location item and the 4 cm ruler item each appear at two different seeds. Six of the fourteen rendered items are therefore duplicates, which is a thin pool for four distinct figures.

competency_alignment.rationale: What varies across seeds is which of the four figures is targeted and whether the probe is by property, by model or by construction, all of which serve this same competency. No item drifts into angles, polygons or other geometry outside its scope.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency sets no numeric ceiling; the only quantities used are endpoint counts of 0, 1 and 2 and ruler marks up to 10 cm, both of which are correct magnitudes for figure properties and for a Grade 3 ruler.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Both verbs are exercised. Recognition appears through models such as the two vertical side segments of the letter H and the segments of the letter T, and drawing is directly addressed by the technique item whose key is to slide the set square along the straight edge of the ruler and draw along its side.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Parallel, intersecting and perpendicular each appear as keys multiple times, and the generator also produces the case that distinguishes them, an item asking what to draw for intersecting lines that are not perpendicular, whose key names two straight lines crossing at a slanted angle.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Explanations lean on objects a Grade 3 pupil handles, the two long edges of a ruler and printed capital letters, and the right-angle idea is glossed as a square right angle or square corner rather than assuming formal angle measurement.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Even within a single response widget the item shapes differ substantially: naming from a real object, naming from a symbolic model, choosing a construction technique, and two relational judgements about whether perpendicular lines intersect and whether parallel lines ever do.

competency_alignment.rationale: The harder seeds probe the relationship between the three categories rather than adding difficulty elsewhere, which deepens exactly the classification this competency builds; the tools questions stay tied to drawing the same three line relationships.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: This competency states no numeric range and the items correctly involve no measurement at all, so nothing is over- or under-scaled; the burden stays on geometric relationship rather than on numbers.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Identification and drawing are both present and both anchored on a ruler: comparison items give two segments by their start and end marks and ask whether they are equal, while construction items fix a starting mark and ask at which centimetre mark Segment B must end.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Both answers to the equality question occur, Yes at seed 42 and No at seeds 43 and 46, so the pupil cannot settle into one response. Segments that begin at 0 cm and segments that begin elsewhere on the ruler are both generated, which is the sub-case that actually tests reading length as a difference.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Lengths stay between 2 and 9 cm and the arithmetic is a single addition or subtraction within 14, suitable for Grade 3 Quarter 1. The distractor phrased as being undeterminable without a set square targets a plausible tool confusion rather than introducing new vocabulary.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Three distinct item shapes recur: a yes/no equality judgement, a choose-the-matching-description item listing candidate segments by their endpoints, and a construct-the-endpoint item. Cloze and mcq are both used, so the presentation is not uniform.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty rises by moving the starting mark off zero, which is precisely the conceptual step this competency requires, namely that length is the difference between marks rather than the number the segment ends on.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: All marks referenced fall between 0 and 14 cm, entirely within a standard classroom ruler, so every item can be physically carried out with the tool the competency names.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The competency requires measuring 'using appropriate measuring tools', and no tool is named anywhere in the sample set. Worse, the rendered stem is simply 'What is the mass of the object in g?' with no object, no scale reading and no data of any kind, so as printed there is nothing from which a mass could be determined; the formatters used are cloze and mcq rather than the read type used elsewhere in this packet for figure-based items.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three units in the competency do appear as keys, in grams, kilograms and milligrams. But the measuring-tool clause generates nothing at all, so one of the two things the competency's wording asks for is entirely unrepresented across eight samples.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The reading demanded is a whole number with no decimals or interval interpolation, and the stem is a single short question, which would be within reach for Grade 3 Quarter 2 if the measurement information were present.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: There is exactly one stem in the entire node, differing only in the three-letter unit. No word problem, no named object, no balance or weighing scale context, and no alternate orientation such as being given a mass and asked which tool suits it.

competency_alignment.rationale: Progression across seeds consists solely of enlarging the number, from 7 up to 1927, while the act required of the pupil stays identical. That is varying numeral magnitude rather than developing measurement skill, and it collides with the physical meaning of the units.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: A mass of 307 kg and a mass of 1927 mg are not quantities a Grade 3 pupil measures with a classroom instrument, and the distractors sit one or two units either side of the key, so the options for the 1927 mg item run 1926 through 1929 and discriminate nothing about mass.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: In every multiple-choice item only one option is a multiple of the stated rounding unit. For the 7 g item the options are 11, 9, 10 and 12, and for the 1927 mg item they are 1999, 2002, 2001 and 2000, so a pupil who has never rounded anything can pick the single round number and be right every time. The rounding the competency is about is never actually required.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three units appear as keys and three different rounding units are generated, to the nearest 10, 100 and 1000, with both rounding up and rounding down occurring, for example 31 g going down to 30 and 26 g going up to 30.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Rounding to the nearest 1000 on a four-digit milligram reading sits at the edge of Grade 3 Quarter 2, and the stem asks the pupil to accept an object measured to 1927 mg, a precision that no Grade 3 estimation activity would produce.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: One frame is used for all thirteen samples, and the object is never anything but an unnamed object. Nothing asks a pupil to choose a sensible benchmark mass for a real item, which is the form estimation normally takes at this level.

competency_alignment.rationale: Because the exact mass is supplied in the stem, the competency's verb of estimating collapses into a pure number-rounding exercise that belongs to the number-sense strand; no item asks the pupil to judge a mass without being told it first.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Seed 600 gives an object measuring 4 mg and a key of 0, which asserts that a real object has a mass of about zero milligrams. The generator's lower bound is not compatible with the rounding unit it pairs with it, and the 307 kg and 1927 mg cases are similarly outside plausible object masses.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Most items can be answered without comparing anything, because only one of the two quantities in the stem ever appears among the options. 'Which is heavier: 19 g or 51 g?' offers 50, 53, 51 and 52, so 51 is the only value the stem actually mentioned; the same holds for the 2 g against 22 g item and the 420 kg against 434 kg item. Picking the option that was in the question suffices.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The competency explicitly includes the use of a balance scale, and no balance appears in any of the fourteen samples. Nor is any object ever named, so 'masses of objects' is reduced to bare numerals with a unit appended, and every single item asks which is heavier, never which is lighter.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Comparing whole numbers within the thousands is within Grade 3 Quarter 2 reach, and pairs are given in the same unit throughout so no conversion, which would be beyond this competency, is ever demanded.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: A single stem frame covers the whole node, with only the two numbers and the unit changing. There is no balance-scale depiction, no three-way ordering, no real object, and no item asking by how much one mass exceeds another.

competency_alignment.rationale: Difficulty is modulated by how far apart the two masses are and how many digits they have, from 2 kg against 3 kg up to 3200 mg against 4228 mg. Since the option set already gives the answer away, neither the close pairs nor the large ones actually test comparison.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Masses of 4228 mg and 434 kg are far from the range a balance scale in a Grade 3 classroom handles, and the near-miss option spreads, 4227 through 4230 for instance, place the burden on reading digits rather than on judging which mass is greater.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: As rendered, 'What is the capacity of the container in L?' supplies no container, no graduation and no reading, so there is nothing in the item from which a capacity could be measured. The competency's requirement to use appropriate measuring tools produces no graduated cylinder, measuring jug or any other instrument in any of the eight samples.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Litres and millilitres both occur as keys, so the unit pair is covered, but the tool clause of the competency generates nothing whatsoever and there is no item distinguishing when litres are the sensible unit and when millilitres are.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Only whole-number readings are asked for, with no fractional graduations or part-filled containers, which would be the appropriate simplification for Grade 3 Quarter 2 had a reading actually been presented.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Eight samples share one stem that varies only between the two units. No pouring situation, no comparison of a container against a labelled litre bottle, and no alternate presentation of any kind is generated.

competency_alignment.rationale: The only axis that moves across seeds is the size of the numeral, from 14 up to 2893, while the demand on the pupil is unchanged. Enlarging the number does not make measuring capacity harder in any way this competency cares about.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: A container of 285 L or 192 L is not something a Grade 3 pupil measures with a classroom tool, and the options are consistently the key plus or minus one or two, as with 284, 286 and 287 around 285, which tests numeral discrimination rather than capacity.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Asking a third grader to accept a container measured as exactly 2893 mL and then round it to the nearest thousand mixes a precision no classroom vessel offers with a rounding unit at the top of the grade's range.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Every sample repeats the same single sentence about an unnamed container, with only the numeral, the unit and the rounding target changing. competency_alignment.rationale: Because the capacity is stated exactly in the stem, the estimating verb of the competency is discharged entirely by a rounding rule, so the progression tracks numeral size rather than any growing sense of how much a litre or millilitre is.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Capacities of 285 L and 192 L do not correspond to containers within a Grade 3 pupil's experience, and pairing such values with the near-miss options 299, 301 and 302 further removes the item from realistic capacity estimation.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The comparison is routinely short-circuited by the options.
